status: source-only design; no product/API edit, build, GPU run or support claim
decision: Keep the public semantic graph. Put its composite implementation in the existing native CUDA Provider, exposed to Graph through its existing region-extension protocol. Do not implement this inside the ggml executor or extend LightningIndexer.

basis.scope: Selected GA dense BF16 index scores. Projection, RoPE/Hadamard/FP4-QAT, persistent cache writes, all-reduce, TopK, invalid-ID replacement and offset remain caller graphs/state operations. Hyle's 68-byte row-cache bank is not the official BF16 cache format.

inputs.K: BF16 [B,L,D]; dense D and key rows, with truthful optional batch pitch larger than L*D*2
inputs.mask: Optional F16 [MB,T,L], MB=1 or B; use the graph's actual Cast(BF16) before Add, never infer mask values

sequence: View reshape W -> [B,T,H,1]; Binary Multiply -> BF16 [B,T,H,L]
Optional mask Cast(BF16) then Binary Add -> BF16 [B,T,L]
Optional final Cast(F32) is an exact widen of the already-rounded BF16 score
public_graph.boundaries: Dot, weighted product, head sum, mask Cast and final Add each retain their own BF16 RNE. The composite may change private physical scratch order, not these visible arithmetic boundaries. MatMul/Reduce require F32 accumulation, not a particular vendor reduction tree.
public_graph.shape_rules: H,D positive; B,T,L may be zero. Batch-specific K must not be flattened into one shared key matrix. A prefix cache keeps its original batch stride. No fixed profile TopK, model ID, H64 or D128 belongs in common infer.
infer_evidence: src/compute_ops/operation.cc:292-364 infer_reshape preserves contiguous chunks and singleton axes across a batch gap
src/compute_ops/operation.cc:580-617 infer_matmul accepts the same-dtype batched BF16 expression without a dense-layout or nonempty restriction
src/compute_ops/operation.cc:1276-1306 Cast, Unary and Binary retain their declared type boundaries
src/compute_ops/operation.cc:1345-1397 Reduce supports the required axis, BF16 output and F32 accumulation
public_graph.public_change_required: None established for this expression. No new public/model_ops descriptor, schema exception or common Graph matcher is needed.

actual_leaf_gaps.fact: The current CUDA ggml MatMul RHS gate accepts dense or matrix-transposed-dense layouts, not a prefix batch gap; representability rejects empty tensors. Ordinary Relu is not admitted/lowered there. Native ggml fmaxf Relu would suppress NaN, so opening that case without preserving its contract is insufficient.
actual_leaf_gaps.consequence: A new region must qualify the complete typed pattern independently of ggml supported_node/eligible flags. Unsupported ordinary fallback for a padded/empty leaf is a backend gap, not missing public mathematics.

actual_leaf_gaps.fact: Existing native CUDA tensor and reduction programs already provide BF16 store RNE, NaN-preserving Relu, BF16 weighted product and F32 head sum followed by BF16 RNE.
actual_leaf_gaps.consequence: Reuse these kernels and the existing Lt BF16-output tile plan; do not route GA through the old all-F32 LightningIndexer.

existing_seams: include/hyle/graph/region_provider.h:153-194,274-306,474-494: bounded cold proposal, exact resources and compile callbacks; Graph validates candidate contraction and original effects
src/graph/executable.cc:5531-5532,5591-5751: discovery queries each retained Provider instance's Region extension; no separate registry is needed
src/compute/provider_internal.h:116-151,216-226: same-build ProviderVTable and ProviderAccess::with_vtable preserve the configured provider payload and lifetime hooks
include/hyle/compute/detail/provider_extension.h:12-24,64-95: original Context retention/admission and exact Queue ownership are already supplied by the extension bridge
src/compute_provider_cuda/cuda_provider.cc:39-53,423-449: native context is the original CUcontext, and query_extension currently serves RowCacheColdPlanning only
src/compute_route_cuda/cuda_context.cc:21-54 and default_context.h:10: existing private default-roster assembly constructs the native Provider; Graph currently injects only its ggml Provider
placement.small_adapter: Add one private region adapter TU/header to graph_route_cuda. Its Provider decoration copies the original native vtable and overrides only query_extension: return the static region table for kRegionProviderExtensionId, otherwise delegate to the original callback. Keep create_context/propose/prepare/drain and configuration retain/release unchanged. Do not wrap the raw native CUcontext in an incompatible state object. Retain the exact original Provider identity/inline configuration and its owning configuration hooks; the configured vtable and both extension tables have static lifetime. This is a capability decoration of the same Provider, not a replacement identity. Delegate every unhandled extension ID to the original query callback, including RowCacheColdPlanning.
placement.assembly: Allow the existing private compute::cuda::internal::create_context assembly to receive a native Provider override (alongside the current ggml argument). Direct keeps cuda_native::provider(); Graph supplies the decorated native instance. Preserve provider ordering/default-policy decoration and the RowCacheColdPlanning extension. Add the real graph_route_cuda -> compute_provider_cuda private module edge; do not add a new module or public factory.
placement.private_operation: A small same-build DenseBfloatScores descriptor in compute_provider_cuda describes this composite's actual output type/mask form and validates its real TensorDesc ports. It is not public model_ops, has no model fields, and is prepared by the existing native CUDA Provider's propose/prepare dispatch. Shape facts come from ports, not duplicated B/T/H/D constants.
placement.prepared_artifact: Region compile converts exact original ports/resources into this private operation and delegates to the original native Provider proposal/prepare. The region wrapper retains the returned ProviderPrepared and its original ProviderPreparedVTable. create_invocation/destroy/shared_submit forward to that table and the original QueueSequence. No nested public Context, extra Queue, Completion polling loop or alternate executor.
placement.meaning_of_fusion: One composite prepared region need not be one physical kernel: the initial implementation may use Lt + typed tensor/reduction + final publish per key tile. Report actual dispatches/workspace; candidate selection is not proof of physical fusion.

implementation_checklist.functions: Factor the existing Part/Cold tile-plan configuration and typed post-dot stages into a small private helper; parameterize H/D from actual shapes. Keep packed/paged mapping, decode, checked ranges, 68-byte format and their Completion errors in their current wrappers. Add dense typed-score select/propose/prepare/create_invocation/shared_submit in the same provider family.
implementation_checklist.rules: Dense K is read directly with its actual batch pitch; no full-history decode/copy. Tile workspace is bounded by the existing 256-key policy and checked dimensions. LT algorithms must support BF16 operands and BF16 D with F32 accumulation. Actual algorithm/stride/alignment limits may decline a shape; do not replace those limits with a model whitelist. A short B loop or checked strided batch may reuse scratch. General H/D are inferred, while existing packed schema continues its fixed H64/D128 contract.

implementation_checklist.functions: Add only a dense score-publish variant: read BF16 head-sum, optionally cast F16 mask to BF16 and widen that rounded value, add in F32 then BF16-RNE, and optionally exact-widen the rounded result to F32. Keep old interval/paged publish untouched.
implementation_checklist.rules: Use actual [B,T,L] output and MB mask broadcast. No inferred 0/-Inf optimization, implicit scaling, interval conversion, TopK or finite guard. Numeric NaN/Inf remains successful numeric output; bounds failures remain explicit Completion errors.

implementation_checklist.functions: Own the private descriptor/infer and route ID, and dispatch its propose/prepare through the current native Provider. Preserve every existing public operation route and projected RowCache access table.
implementation_checklist.rules: Every byte count, B*L*D and tile product, stride, native int field, offset and launch grid must be overflow checked. Return a genuine zero-work prepared artifact before payload pointer/Lt allocation for an empty result. Do not require nonempty Q/K/W payload for B/T/L=0.

implementation_checklist.functions: Implement whole-pattern match/propose_resources/compile plus the thin Provider extension decoration and native Provider injection at existing context assembly.
implementation_checklist.rules: Follow actual ValueIds, legal View descriptors and accumulation settings. Require allowed_nodes and exact closed single-result intermediate use/output/alias/control contracts. Optional mask/add/final-widen suffixes may be absorbed only when private; otherwise keep their real graph boundary. Never require unsupported leaves to be pre-admitted by ggml. No CONT stripping, same-address value substitution or model/workload lookup. Use bounded allocator-backed cold indices and truthful compilation/persistent/invocation workspace counts.

lifetime_and_layout: Use original Graph resources/ReadLease/StorageOwner admission. Cache no ready permission or caller TensorView address beyond the ordinary binding contract; Queue replacement and Context close retain their current checks.

All mutable Lt handles/scratch belong to the existing invocation. Shared immutable descriptions/plans may be prepared state. Partial vendor acceptance returns accepted-prefix semantics through QueueSequence; a numeric nonfinite result is not a provider failure.

Start with dense Q/W, actual K row-dense plus batch pitch, and exact supported mask layouts. General strided operands are not claimed. Restrict output/input overlap unless explicitly implemented; retain original allocation and published-alias protection.

Capture compatibility is a separately qualified property of the dense prepared path. Do not inherit the paged path's noncapture status or claim capture from a selected route. Workspace is caller-owned, and hot submit must not plan/allocate or create another execution sequence.
small_regression_plan: One arithmetic fixture embeds the independent dyadic dot-RNE, product-RNE and head-sum-RNE witnesses in a nonzero small H/D problem; use the previous review's exact expected values. Add the F16 mask-Cast witness score=-1, mask=1+2^-10: CastBF16 then Add must yield 0, not 2^-10. NaN classification is checked independently of Completion success.

One Graph fixture uses two invocations/slots, two rounds with fresh addresses and retained old outputs; B=2 K has a larger physical batch pitch and distinct batches. Include optional mask and final F32 widen, ordinary dense B=1 published-reader/control escape rejection, and B/T/L=0 no-read behavior in the same small table. Use a native+ordinary-default provider context for fallback tests, since ggml alone does not currently provide NaN-correct Relu.

Compare against the explicitly staged public BF16 operators and the independent dyadic oracle. Do not demand arbitrary Lt-vs-Torch reduction bit identity. Retain original packed RowCache empty/checked-range tests to prove factoring did not change that contract.

Only after implementation: actual source-owner incremental host/native compile, directed CUDA cases and physical dispatch/capture evidence. This design does not assert all four backends, complete GA model execution, quality or speed.
unresolved_and_not_claimed: The exact first dense implementation's LT H/D/stride/alignment admissible domain requires real proposal/compile qualification; broad public infer does not assert every backend accepts it.
CPU/Apple/Vulkan could recognize the same public expression later; current view/cast/empty eligibility differs. This CUDA plan does not mark those custom integrations implemented.
GA all-reduce and cache-state ownership remain outside this local scorer. Selected official sources prescribe visible dtype stages but not one universal physical F32 dot/head-reduction tree.
No descriptor extension to the existing F32 LightningIndexer and no reinterpretation of the packed RowCache bank is proposed.
